edge_cases: Missing or empty "username" or "password" fields cause a server error (KeyError).
Providing a username that already exists yields "user already exists" without altering the database.
SQL injection is possible because the query concatenates raw input.
Database connection failures raise an exception and produce a 500 response.
Empty strings are accepted as valid credentials and will be stored as such.
contract.intent: Create a new user account by handling a POST request to the /register endpoint.
invariants: Usernames are unique; duplicate usernames are never inserted.
Passwords are stored only as a SHA‑1 hash of the supplied value.
The endpoint always returns one of the two fixed response strings.
io_behavior: Accepts an HTTP POST with form fields "username" and "password".
Returns the plain‑text string "register success" when a new account is created.
Returns the plain‑text string "user already exists" when the username is already present.
side_effects: Opens a connection to a MySQL database.
Inserts a new row into the "user" table on successful registration.
Commits the transaction to persist the new user record.

rationale: Core success and duplicate paths work, but missing/empty fields, empty credentials, SQL injection resistance, password hashing method, and extra error responses violate the contract; only side‑effects match fully.
